result:
Parking the roadmap: 1 of 2 committed stages is complete. Stage 2 and the three Ranked-list items (O2, O3, O4) go to the deferred backlog, and the roadmap moves to `specs/completed/`. You asked for the whole roadmap, so Stage 2 (closure notices, Track B) parks too, even though it doesn't depend on the study.

These are the tool calls I'll run, in order:

**1. Read the item schema and the existing backlog before writing anything**
```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/references/deferred-backlog.md   # Deferred-item schema
Read specs/deferred_items.md                                          # create it if absent
```

**2. Append one section with four items**, each in that schema, self-contained, with `Size:` and `Done when:`:
```
## lock-closures — 2026-11-06

- [ ] Closure notices (was Stage 2, Track B)
      Email boat operators within an hour of a lock closing, from the closure log's live feed.
      Size: small (one closure-log poll every 10 minutes)
      Done when: the notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every
      address on the list within an hour of a new closure entry.

- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (was Ranked list A #1, O2)
      Apply Stage 1's response curve (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md) to the river-level forecast.
      Size: small (one model run a day; Stage 1's fit took 22 min on a laptop)
      Done when: a 7-day closure-risk outlook for each lock is produced from the real river-level forecast.

- [ ] Per-lock closure curves, pooled (was Ranked list A #2, O3)
      Separate closure curves for all 14 locks, pooled across locks.
      Size: medium (about 14× Stage 1's 1.8 GB, roughly 25 GB)
      Done when: a closure curve for each of the 14 locks, fit on real data, is recorded with its measured run cost.

- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (was Ranked list A #3, O4)
      A static map page of each lock's closure history.
      Size: small (about a day of work)
      Done when: boat operators can open a map page showing each lock's closure history.
```
If the schema asks for fields I haven't shown here (for example, an origin line), I'll fill them from the roadmap.

**3. Retire the roadmap**
```
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
Edit: under the title, add
  > PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete. Funding for the canal study ended.
  > Remaining stage and Ranked-list items: specs/deferred_items.md, "lock-closures — 2026-11-06".
```
This roadmap had no source spec, so there are no methodology or critique files to retire with it. The Stage 1 findings file stays in `specs/` as the record of what was learned.

**4. Commit on `main`** (local only, no push)
```
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap: 1 of 2 stages complete; remaining items deferred"
```

Text-message notices were listed in Stage 2's `Leaves out` with nothing picking them up. They aren't a stage or a Ranked-list item, so they don't park. Tell me if you want a deferred item for them too.

After the commit, nothing is routed and the roadmap is closed. If funding returns, the deferred items are the place to start. O2 is the cheapest of them, since Stage 1's curve already exists.
